steps.title: Prepare reverse transcription mix
steps.instruction: To 5 µL of aRNA add 1 µL random hexamer primer (20 µM, final 3.07 µM) and 0.5 µL dNTP mix (10 mM, final 0.77 mM) for a total volume of 6.5 µL.

steps.title: Denature aRNA
steps.instruction: Heat the mixture at 65 °C for 5 min, then place immediately on ice.

steps.title: Add reverse transcription part 2
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL 5× First‑strand buffer (final 0.95×), 1 µL 0.1 M DTT (final 9.5 mM), 0.5 µL RNaseOUT (40 U/µL, final 1.9 U/µL) and 0.5 µL SuperScript II (200 U/µL, final 9.5 U/µL) to reach a total volume of 10.5 µL.

steps.title: Reverse transcription incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate at 25 °C for 10 min, then 42 °C for 1 h, and hold at 4 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Set up PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Transfer 5.25 µL of the reverse‑transcribed aRNA to a new PCR tube (store the remaining 5.25 µL at –20 °C). Add 1 µL RP1 primer (10 µM, final 0.40 µM), 1 µL indexed RNA PCR primer (10 µM, final 0.40 µM), 12.5 µL NEBNext high‑fidelity 2× PCR mix (final 0.99×) and 5.5 µL nuclease‑free water, bringing the volume to 25.25 µL.

steps.title: Run PCR program
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat thermocycler to 98 °C, then insert tubes and run: 98 °C 30 s (initial denaturation), 98 °C 10 s (denaturation) for 8–14 cycles, 60 °C 30 s (annealing), 72 °C 30 s (extension), 72 °C 10 min (final extension), hold at 4 °C forever.

steps.title: Post‑PCR water addition
steps.instruction: Briefly spin tubes, add 24.75 µL nuclease‑free water, and transfer the mixture to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: First AMPure XP cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 41.25 µL AMPure XP beads (0.825×) to the 50 µL PCR product, incubate 15 min, place on magnetic stand, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with freshly prepared 80 % ethanol, air‑dry 3–10 min, elute in 50 µL nuclease‑free water for 10 min, separate on magnet and transfer supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Second AMPure XP cleanup
steps.instruction: Repeat the 0.825× bead cleanup on the eluate from step 8, but elute in 15 µL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Assess library size
steps.instruction: Load 1 µL of each library onto an Agilent High‑Sensitivity DNA chip and run the Bioanalyzer according to the manufacturer’s protocol; verify that >90 % of fragments are 200–1000 bp with minimal primer (<100 bp) or dimer (~120 bp) peaks.

steps.title: Quantify library concentration
steps.instruction: Measure 1 µL of each library with the Qubit dsDNA High‑Sensitivity assay; typical concentrations range from 0.5 to 4 ng/µL.

steps.title: Pool and sequence libraries
steps.instruction: Combine libraries that carry distinct indexed PCR primers (RPI1‑RPI48) and sequence on an Illumina platform to a depth of ~0.5–1 million reads per cell, using at least 76 cycles for read 1; no custom sequencing primers are required.

steps.title: Optional storage pause point
steps.instruction: Samples may be stored at –20 °C after reverse transcription or after PCR (before or after the AMPure XP cleanups).

description: This protocol for scH&G-seq (Single-cell 5-hydroxymethylcytosine and genomic DNA sequencing) was recently developed in a publication to simultaneously quantify 5hmC and genomic DNA from a single cell (Wangsanuwat et al., 2021). scH&G-seq builds upon scAba-Seq (Mooijman et al., 2016), where the addition of restriction enzymes BseRI and/or AluI enables sequencing of genomic DNA together with 5hmC in single cells. BseRI was selected because it generates the same overhang after digestion of genomic DNA as AbaSI, which is used to detect 5hmC. In addition, the recognition sequence of BseRI is devoid of CpG, eliminating ambiguity in assigning reads to genomic DNA or 5hmC. Thus, both genomic DNA-derived reads and 5hmC-derived reads can be separated computationally post-sequencing while being ligated and amplified from the same double-stranded adapter. AluI was selected to increase the coverage of the genome, as described previously (Rooijers et al., 2019). As digestion with AluI leaves a blunt end, an additional blunt double-stranded adapter is required to capture genomic DNA reads derived from AluI. The AluI double-stranded adapters and AbaSI/BseRI double-stranded adapters use different sets of unique barcodes. This protocol provides step-by-step instructions for performing scH&G-seq using both BseRI and AluI simultaneously. It also includes modifications to the protocol if only one of the two enzymes are used. Finally, scH&G-seq can be performed on any cell type that can be sorted by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) and has 5hmC in its genome. The scH&G-seq protocol is completed over several days. Day 1 in the table below is the day a sorted 384-well plate containing single cells is thawed from −80°C for use in the scH&G-seq protocol.
